newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel recommends more share sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: India panel recommends more share sell-offs.

text.p: India's Disinvestment Commission has recommended the sale of shares in six state firms, in addition to the three in which it sought sell-offs earlier this year, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

The new companies named are the Bharat Aluminium Company (BALCO), telecommunications firm ITI Ltd, Bongaigaon Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd (BRPL), teleprinter maker HTL Ltd, Madras Fertilisers Ltd (MFL) and Manganese Ore India Ltd (MOIL), the news agency said.
PTI said the commission had recommended the sale of 100 percent of the equity in HTL, up to 74 percent in BALCO, ITI and and BRPL and 50 percent in MFL and MOIL.

Government officials confirmed to Reuters the recommendations of the commission, which was set up last year to advise on the modalities of sales under a partial privatisation programme forming part of economic reforms launched in 1991.

In view of the real estate and other values associated with some state companies, the commission had recommended a minimum reserve price for these units, PTI quoted Commission Chairman G.V. Ramakrishna as saying.
The commission has recommended an immediate divestment of 40 percent of the equity of BALCO to a strategic partner, through a strategic partner, PTI said.
In BRPL, the commission recommended the sale of 50 percent of equity immediately to Indian or foreign oil companies either on their own or in association with one another, it said.

"There could be an agreement with the selected strategic partners specifying further dilution of government equity to 26 percent or below through a domestic public offer," it quoted the commission as saying.

In order to attract sufficient interest among bidders, the government should make a policy statement laying down a two-year time-frame for deregulation of state controls on petroleum prices, the commission was quoted as saying.

The commission in its first report earlier in February recommended a divestment strategy for three companies, the Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL), the India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC) and Modern Food Industries Ltd.
The government is yet to take a decision on them.

The Indian government, in its budget for 1997/98 (April-March), proposed to raise 48 billion rupees from the sale of shares in state-owned firms during the year, compared with a target of 50 billion for 1996/97.
